Each square that is contained in both an even-numbered row and an even-numbered column is cut out. A small section of the grid is shown below, with the cut-out squares in black. Compute the maximum number of $L$-triominoes (pictured below) that can be placed in the grid so that each $L$-triomino lies entirely inside the grid and no two overlap. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a small labeled square grid, with black cut-out squares occurring where the row label and column label are both even. To the right, the pictured L-triomino consists of three unit squares forming a 2-by-2 block with one corner missing; the problem states that rotations are allowed. Reasoning: Any L-triomino occupies exactly three cells of some adjacent 2-by-2 block. In any adjacent pair of rows and adjacent pair of columns, one row is odd and one is even, and one column is odd and one is even, so the 2-by-2 block contains exactly one even-row/even-column cell, which is cut out. Therefore a valid L-triomino must occupy the other three parity types: one odd-row/odd-column cell, one odd-row/even-column cell, and one even-row/odd-column cell. There are 51 odd-numbered rows and 50 even-numbered rows, and likewise 51 odd-numbered columns and 50 even-numbered columns. Thus there are 51·50 = 2550 odd-row/even-column cells and 50·51 = 2550 even-row/odd-column cells. Since each L-triomino uses one of each of these types, at most 2550 L-triominoes can be placed. To attain this, index the odd rows and odd columns by i,j = 1,...,51, forming a 51-by-51 array of odd-row/odd-column cells. Leave the 51 diagonal odd-odd cells unused. For every off-diagonal odd-odd cell (i,j), place one L-triomino using that cell and the two adjacent connector cells toward the diagonal: if j < i, use the adjacent odd-row/even-column cell to the right and the adjacent even-row/odd-column cell above; if j > i, use the adjacent odd-row/even-column cell to the left and the adjacent even-row/odd-column cell below. Each such placement avoids the cut-out even-even cell. Checking connectors, an odd-row/even-column cell between odd columns t and t+1 in odd row i is used exactly once: by (i,t) if t < i, otherwise by (i,t+1). Similarly, an even-row/odd-column cell between odd rows s and s+1 in odd column j is used exactly once: by (s+1,j) if j ≤ s, otherwise by (s,j). Hence there is no overlap, and the number of placed triominoes is 51^2 - 51 = 2550, matching the upper bound.

method.method_draft: Begin from the visual: the sample shows that every 2-by-2 block with one even row and one even column has the even-even square cut out, leaving an L-shape matching the pictured triomino. From the text, set 101=2*50+1. Prove an upper bound by observing that every valid L-triomino must contain exactly one cell whose row is odd and column is even; there are 51*50=2550 such cells, so the answer is at most 2550. For the construction, prove the more general case for a (2m+1) by (2m+1) board by building outward in rings. Start with the 1 by 1 board and no triominoes. When extending from size 2t-1 to size 2t+1, add rows 2t, 2t+1 and columns 2t, 2t+1. Place t Ls along the new bottom band: for each k=1,...,t, use the three non-cut cells in the 2-by-2 block with rows 2t,2t+1 and columns 2k-1,2k. Place another t Ls along the new right band: for each k=1,...,t, use the three non-cut cells in the 2-by-2 block with rows 2k-1,2k and columns 2t,2t+1. These new Ls do not overlap except at cut-out squares, which are absent, and they leave only the new corner odd-odd cell uncovered in that ring. Thus the number placed after t=50 is sum_{t=1}^{50} 2t=50*51=2550, achieving the upper bound.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中左侧的小网格按行、列标号，黑色方格出现在偶数行与偶数列的交点处；右侧给出的 L-triomino 是一个由 2×2 方格去掉一个角后剩下的 3 个小方格组成的 L 形。图示支持这样一个结构：每个相邻的 2×2 小块中，若包含一个偶数行、偶数列的黑色删去格，则其余三个格正好形成一个 L-triomino。

再推理：因为 101=2·50+1，所以奇数行有 51 行，偶数列有 50 列。考虑任意一个合法放置的 L-triomino。它必然占据某个 2×2 方格块中的 3 个格。任意连续两行和连续两列组成的 2×2 块中，恰有一个格是偶数行、偶数列，因此这个格被挖掉。合法 L-triomino 不能覆盖被挖掉的格，所以它必须正好使用该 2×2 块中另外三个格。于是每个合法 L-triomino 都恰好包含一个“奇数行、偶数列”的格。

这样的奇数行、偶数列格共有 51×50=2550 个。由于不同 L-triomino 不重叠，每个 L-triomino 都要消耗一个这样的格，所以最多只能放 2550 个。

下面构造达到这个上界。更一般地，对 (2m+1)×(2m+1) 棋盘逐圈构造。初始 1×1 棋盘不放任何 L。假设已经构造到大小 2t−1，再扩展到大小 2t+1，即新增第 2t、2t+1 行和第 2t、2t+1 列。沿新增的底部带状区域，对 k=1,2,...,t，在行 2t,2t+1 与列 2k−1,2k 形成的 2×2 块中放入其三个未删去格，得到 t 个 L。沿新增的右侧带状区域，对 k=1,2,...,t，在行 2k−1,2k 与列 2t,2t+1 形成的 2×2 块中放入其三个未删去格，得到另外 t 个 L。这些 L 之间不会重叠；可能相接的地方只是偶数行、偶数列的删去格，而这些格本来不存在。该圈只留下新的右下角奇奇格未覆盖。

因此从 t=1 到 t=50，总共可放置的 L-triomino 数量为 ∑_{t=1}^{50}2t=50·51=2550。上界可达到，所以最大值为 2550。

raw_record.original_question: A $101\times 101$ square grid is given with rows and columns numbered in order from $1$ to $101$. Each square that is contained in both an even-numbered row and an even-numbered column is cut out. A small section of the grid is shown below, with the cut-out squares in black. Compute the maximum number of $L$-triominoes that can be placed in the grid so that each $L$-triomino lies entirely inside the grid and no two overlap. Each $L$-triomino may be placed in the orientation pictured below, or rotated by $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$, or $270^\circ$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a small labeled square grid, with black cut-out squares occurring where the row label and column label are both even. To the right, the pictured L-triomino consists of three unit squares forming a 2-by-2 block with one corner missing; the problem states that rotations are allowed. Reasoning: Any L-triomino occupies exactly three cells of some adjacent 2-by-2 block. In any adjacent pair of rows and adjacent pair of columns, one row is odd and one is even, and one column is odd and one is even, so the 2-by-2 block contains exactly one even-row/even-column cell, which is cut out. Therefore a valid L-triomino must occupy the other three parity types: one odd-row/odd-column cell, one odd-row/even-column cell, and one even-row/odd-column cell. There are 51 odd-numbered rows and 50 even-numbered rows, and likewise 51 odd-numbered columns and 50 even-numbered columns. Thus there are 51·50 = 2550 odd-row/even-column cells and 50·51 = 2550 even-row/odd-column cells. Since each L-triomino uses one of each of these types, at most 2550 L-triominoes can be placed. To attain this, index the odd rows and odd columns by i,j = 1,...,51, forming a 51-by-51 array of odd-row/odd-column cells. Leave the 51 diagonal odd-odd cells unused. For every off-diagonal odd-odd cell (i,j), place one L-triomino using that cell and the two adjacent connector cells toward the diagonal: if j < i, use the adjacent odd-row/even-column cell to the right and the adjacent even-row/odd-column cell above; if j > i, use the adjacent odd-row/even-column cell to the left and the adjacent even-row/odd-column cell below. Each such placement avoids the cut-out even-even cell. Checking connectors, an odd-row/even-column cell between odd columns t and t+1 in odd row i is used exactly once: by (i,t) if t < i, otherwise by (i,t+1). Similarly, an even-row/odd-column cell between odd rows s and s+1 in odd column j is used exactly once: by (s+1,j) if j ≤ s, otherwise by (s,j). Hence there is no overlap, and the number of placed triominoes is 51^2 - 51 = 2550, matching the upper bound.
